text.p: Fisher Scientific Inc said on Thursday it would merge with a unit of Thomas H Lee in a $1.4 billion recapitalization which reduces existing shareholders common stock ownership in the company to 10.3 percent from 100 percent.
Other investors in the deal include DLJ Merchant Banking Partners and Chase Capital Partners, Fisher said.
A Fisher spokespman said Thomas H Lee would be the largest shareholder in the recapitallized company, but that the size of Lee's, DLJ's and Chase's stakes were not disclosed.

The announcements accompanied the release of the company's second quarter earnings. The company reported second quarter diluted net of $0.46 a share vs $0.46 a share in the same period a year earlier.
In the same statement, the company said a prolonged UPS strike could have an "adverse impact on future results of the company."
Fisher said under the terms of the recapitalization, 97 percent of the fully diluted common shares will be converted into the right to receive $51.00 per share in cash, or an aggregate $1.06 billion.
The remaining three percent of the shares will be retained by existing stockholders, and will represent about 10.3 percent of the common stock ownership in the company, the statement said.

Consummation of the merger is subject, among other things, to Company stockholder approval at a special stockholder meeting to be held in late November or early December 1997, receipt of the necessary financing and customary conditions including the absence of a material adverse change to the Company.
The financing necessary for the transaction has been fully committed by The Chase Manhattan Bank and Merrill Lynch & Co, the company said.

"We are delighted and look forward to having Thomas H. Lee Company as a new investor in Fisher. Our Board conducted an extensive process for the purpose of developing a favorable financial alternative for the Fisher stockholders. This transaction allows stockholders to receive cash for most of their shares at a very attractive price," said Fisher chief executive Paul Montrone. "We believe that the agreement we are announcing today demonstrates Thomas H. Lee Company's confidence in the future of Fisher."
